current_text.html: Scriptural law is the basis of all discipline because it is the revelation of God's Holy will. Proper disciplinary principles are set forth in the Scriptures and must be followed. They are: a. Instruction in the Word; b. Individual's responsibility to admonish one another (Matthew 18:15, Galatians 6:1); c. If the admonition is rejected, then the calling of one or more witnesses (Matthew 18:16); d. If rejection persists, then the Church must act through her court unto admonition, suspension, excommunication and deposition (See BCO 29 and 30 for further explanation). Steps (a) through (d) must be followed in proper order for the exercise of discipline.

relationships.title: Voluntary resignation from membership and application of BCO 46-5

occurrences.excerpt: The GA clarified that BCO 46-5 had been variously interpreted regarding voluntary resignation, resolving that a simple resignation does not automatically trigger the willful-neglect excommunication process.

relationships.title: Whether a resignation letter constitutes willful neglect justifying roll erasure

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB held that 'deletion' under BCO 46-5 is equivalent to excommunication and referred the question of easier non-judicial removal to the 17th GA for potential BCO amendment.

relationships.title: Informal versus formal admonition and due-process requirements under BCO 27-5

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB distinguished informal admonition (ordinary relational correction) from formal judicial admonition, holding that the paragraph in question did not require BCO 27-5 due process.

relationships.title: Grounds and procedures for removing members from PCA church rolls
relationships.disposition: declined to answer specific questions; general advice given

occurrences.excerpt: Declining to address case-specific questions, the CCB outlined the three BCO provisions by which members may be removed from church rolls: transfer, discipline, or relocation.

relationships.title: Procedure for removing members who relocate without affiliating elsewhere

occurrences.excerpt: BCO 46-2 governs removal of members who move away and fail to affiliate within a year; BCO 46-5's formal discipline applies only to willful neglect, not mere relocation.

relationships.title: Teaching elder voting rights and congregational approval of pastoral salary changes

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB advised that a teaching elder votes as a full session member, and that any change to pastoral salary terms requires congregational approval as part of the call.

relationships.title: Whether deletion from the roll under BCO 46-5 constitutes excommunication

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB answered yes — 'deletion' under BCO 46-5 is excommunication in effect, and the due-process procedures of BCO 27-5 must therefore be followed.

relationships.title: Whether deletion from the roll under BCO 46-5 constitutes excommunication

relationships.title: Meaning of willful neglect and gross crime under BCO 46-5 and 30-4

occurrences.excerpt: BCO 46-5 requires due process under BCO 27-5 for incorrigible members, and 'gross crime or heresy' is to be understood in its biblical and moral sense as determined by the church court.

metadata.synopsis: Grace PCA’s Session challenged Ohio Presbytery’s reversal of excommunication for two members convicted of heresy. The SJC partially sustained the complaint: prior indefinite suspension was not constitutionally required, but Presbytery properly found excommunication too severe because the trial record contained no evidence of contumacy. Presbytery nevertheless had to impose an appropriate lesser censure or remand for one, and lacked authority to mandate transfer to another church. The unappealed heresy convictions remained, but because the members had joined another church, further proceedings were moot.

metadata.synopsis: An excommunicated member appealed the Missouri Presbytery judicial commission's guilty verdict and excommunication, alleging specifications of error. The SJC denied the appeal and did not sustain any specification, holding only that the appellant failed to demonstrate sufficient reason to sustain the alleged errors; the excommunication thus remained in effect. The record noted Presbytery dismissed the commission without the BCO 15-3 vote to approve its report, but the adopted reasoning gave no further explanation and did not address that fact.

relationships.title: Schrock et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery

topics: fundamentals of the system of doctrine
metadata.synopsis: The SJC sustained a complaint against Philadelphia Presbytery for failing to judge and record TE Larry Smith’s stated difference over the continuation of prophecy and tongues beyond the apostolic era. The record showed Presbytery approved Smith’s transfer exam and defeated a motion to find his view out of accord, but it did not categorize that view in Smith’s own words. The SJC remanded for a written statement and Presbytery’s categorical judgment, without undoing Smith’s transfer or deciding whether his view was erroneous.

relationships.title: Morton Smith v. Western Carolina

metadata.synopsis: The complaint challenged Presbytery’s commissions and its response to a canceled congregational meeting. The SJC upheld the Inman Commission because a Session may reference limited duties without congregational consent. It sustained the challenges to Presbytery’s consideration of the August 7 meeting and appointment of the Sealy Commission because the Session majority had validly canceled the meeting. Linton’s and Pellom’s calls therefore remained undissolved and Neville was uncalled, absent later congregational action. The SJC also upheld Presbytery’s criticism of the cancellation as unwise and its refusal to issue a BCO 40-5 citation.

relationships.title: Morton Smith v. Western Carolina

metadata.synopsis: Smith challenged Presbytery’s reversal of a finding that an elder’s race-and-IQ views did not create a strong presumption of guilt and its immediate judgment against those views. The SJC upheld the reversal as a discretionary determination, without addressing its merits, but annulled the declaration against the views because a strong-presumption finding required judicial process. On remand, Presbytery was to commence process against the elder or rescind that finding and drop the matter. The ruling did not restrict Presbytery’s ability to adopt general position statements outside an investigation.

relationships.title: Hathaway v. Grace Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: The Session of the Waynesboro Presbyterian Church refused to take up the proper steps leading either to restoration or excommunication, if necessary, under the provisions of Book of Church Order 27-5, which states:
6. December 11, 1989, the Session postponed consideration of complainant's recommendation that procedures of Book of Church Order 27-5 be instituted in regard to certain named members. (p.42)

metadata.synopsis: TE Vaughn Hathaway complained that the Session of Waynesboro Presbyterian Church failed to institute discipline against seven members who had not attended worship for over a year. The judicial panel denied the complaint on the grounds that the Session retained discretion to determine the timing of discipline proceedings, and procedural errors did not result in material prejudice.
